title: Add a source-shaped Lean bridge for compiler retention
body:
## Contribution

Focused verification follow-up to #3391, in one new package. The original 28-file archive is unchanged; this does not update the selected frontier, a supplier, or the review ledger.

`CompilerAudit.SourceBridge.selected_source_transport` derives **ordered renamed trace equality**, **28,278 N distinct source keys**, **904,896 N retained wrapper identities**, and **1,809,792 N + B direct references** from primitive event-projection, LOW-inverse, block-budget and identity-freshness premises. It does **not** assume the final equality or those totals. Here `N = |GL64(F_q)|`; `B` counts emitted blocks, not native cost.

Start with [README](https://github.com/PellaML/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7bd54e91748eb9fc6b13d61d232b6a91e8158aba/research/selected-compiler-source-bridge/README.md), [CONTRACT](https://github.com/PellaML/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7bd54e91748eb9fc6b13d61d232b6a91e8158aba/research/selected-compiler-source-bridge/CONTRACT.md), and [VALIDATION](https://github.com/PellaML/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7bd54e91748eb9fc6b13d61d232b6a91e8158aba/research/selected-compiler-source-bridge/VALIDATION.md).

## Executed evidence

- [Hosted registered Python CI](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39129982667) **passed at the published head**: planning and explicit bounded package replay succeeded. Lean was checked locally, not in hosted CI.
- CPython 3.12.6: registered normal/`-O` replays pass with identical substantive results; **152 live input pins**. PR3391's scientific digest remains `c1bc50f54937cd3b2efae61bb5b655b55859b3ed7ddcf1a2e9bbd8682fc88f3d`.
- Independent q=3 census: all 32 replicas, **7,843,392 local events**, 28,278 requests and 19 groups, without GL64 enumeration. Tiny original-emitter ordering and wrapper-lifetime controls pass.
- **46 Python control-test methods** and **17 Lean-runner test methods** pass normally and under `-O`.
- Lean 4.34.1: seven predecessor modules plus the bridge compiled freshly; exact bridge/baseline contracts, the fixed 27-name axiom inventory, explicit bridge-module kernel replay and three discriminating probes pass. Only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`; nine dependency source revisions checked. Cached library artifacts remain trusted, not cold-rebuilt.
- Committed-byte/source-history preflight, raw ancestor/source-pin cross-check, checked shared-exporter bundle, and fresh Git-free normal/`-O` replays pass. The exported bridge also passes a fresh Lean replay. **174 payload files plus one export manifest**; no compiled objects or agent scratch reports are included.

## Interpretation and limits

This is a **conditional, idealized/unbounded source-shaped model**, not formal Python semantics or a GL64 codec proof. A complete selected eager list/tuple cannot return on conventional 32/64-bit CPython: at q=3, N has 6,492 bits and the required begin/end entries have 6,512 bits. Other failures may occur earlier; no first-failure, lazy-representation barrier, native/stock tariff, precision result or full multiplication theorem is claimed. `Specifications` already caches records/plans; wrappers are the distinct objects counted here.

Tiny lifetime fixtures bypass loader bootstrap after source-only hash checks and do not test cold 64-dimensional initialization or selected numerical endpoints. The Windows census adapter changes one authenticated inventory-path spelling expression only. The explicit Lean checks are local; hosted CI covers the registered Python commands. Neither constitutes scientific admission.

## Sources, overlap and credit

Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`; publication: `7bd54e91748eb9fc6b13d61d232b6a91e8158aba`. Priority revision 6 and selected conditional kappa **0.001672660197076918** are unchanged. PR3391 remains archival/partially reviewed.

The refreshed overlap pass located #2569's existing **written LOW bijection proof for byte-identical codec source**. The remaining target is implementation-level formal correspondence, not an absent written argument. #2989/#3041/#3223 cover complementary source refinements. Roger Sato's parallel #3634/#3602 address shared axiom-scanner/report issues; this package changes no shared checker and claims no priority for those issues. Tekalign's shared exporter is retained rather than duplicated. Metadata searches were broad, but the all-open changed-file refresh timed out; no exhaustive novelty claim.

Credit is retained for Jose Manuel, David Arias, ywz65, Nick Petalas, Matthieu Pascal, Ross Richardson, Douglas Colkitt and the retained source contributors. Submitted by Kewin Talaga (`PellaML`), with substantial OpenAI Codex, GPT 6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 assistance. Separate AI checks are not independent human certification. Apache-2.0; original notices preserved.
